chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abd al-Malik! Why do I not see you going out to these places that the people of your city go to?' I said, 'And where?' So he said: 'Jeddah, Abadan, al-Massisa, and Qazwin.' I said, 'In anticipation of your command and following you.' So he said: 'Yes, by God! If it were good, they would not have preceded us to it.'

He said: I said to him, 'The Zaydis say there is no difference between us and Ja'far except that he does not consider the jihad.' So he said: 'I do not consider it? Yes, by God, I certainly do consider it, but I abhor that I should abandon my knowledge in favour of their ignorance.'

key_terms.الجهاد: Jihad; here specifically armed military struggle, distinguished from the Imam's principled restraint
key_terms.الزيدية: Zaydis; followers of Zayd ibn Ali who recognized legitimacy of armed rebellion against unjust rulers
key_terms.المواضع: Places; here referring to frontier garrison towns (thugur) on the borders of the Islamic empire
key_terms.انتظاراً لأمركم: In anticipation of your command; awaiting the Imam's authorization for rightful jihad
key_terms.جهلهم: Their ignorance; refers to those who fight without proper Imamic authorization

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about participating in armed jihad during the Abbasid period?
ai.summary: In this narration, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) rebukes Abd al-Malik ibn Amr for not following the practice of his fellow citizens who went out to frontier garrison towns (thugur) like Jeddah, Abadan, al-Massisa, and Qazwin for military jihad. The Imam affirms the principle that if such practices were truly meritorious, those who preceded the Imams would not have done so first. When Abd al-Malik relays the Zaydis' accusation that Ja'far rejects jihad, the Imam categorically denies this, clarifying that his restraint is not from lack of belief in jihad but from refusing to exchange his divinely-guided knowledge for the ignorance of those who would wage unauthorized war.
